newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude to stage corrective bounce.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude to stage corrective bounce.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - June 10 -------------
+ NYMEX crude was expected to stage small, corrective bounce on Tuesday, but few thought any gains would short-lived.
+ July crude resistance at $19.85, $18.96-98 and $19.14-15.
+ Gasoline also seen heading higher with resistance around 57.30/40 cents a gallon.
NYMEX crude futures were pipped to stage a small corrective bounce on Tuesday, although few chartists saw any moves higher being sustained in the longterm.
July crude closed 11 cents lower at $18.68 a barrel on Monday having shed 87 cents on Friday.
July gasoline, meanwhile, ended a 0.93 cent lower at 56.20 a gallon and heat a 0.02 cent easier at 51.50 a gallon.
Most chartists were looking for a small corrective bounce at the open.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International in Gainesville, Georgia expected July crude to rise up to $18.96 and then $19.18, before sinking back to a new low.
"In the coming week or more, we're dealing with a series of unsustainable corrective bounces followed by new lows," he said in his daily global energy outlook.
He pegged resistance for July at $18.96-98, $19.02-$19.04, $19.18 and $19.38-43. He pinpointed support at $18.60-50, $18.14, $17.08 and $15.45.
Chartists also noted that Relative Strength Indices, indicating the ratio of upward to downward movements as a percentage, were looking rather oversold.
The 14-day RSI for July crude stood at 27.76 percent at Monday's close.
Values under 30 generally indicate "oversold" conditions and values above 70 "overbought" conditions.
Analysts at MeesPierson Derivatives were more cautious.
"With a selling extreme now in place and very negative preparation, we have to sell rallies again. Look to sell at $18.85/90, cutting should we cover $18.95," they said in their daily report.

"With such poor preparation we would even join breaks lower beneath $18.55. Of course, we are on the look out for a buying extreme today as an indication that the rout has finally ended and to cover shorts," they said in their report.
Gasoline was xpected to correct higher in the short-term.
"The next move of consequence is probably a significant corrective bounce starting from little under 56.10 that carries above 57.60 and towards 58.60ish," Graham said.
He pegged resistance at 57.60-80, 58.60ish and 60.15 cents while support was seen at 56.10-55.80-ish and 51.00ish.
MeesPierson, meanwhile, were looking to remain short and continue selling up to 57.00 cents, covering shorts after 57.30 cents.
They pegged support at 56.10 cents and resistance at 57.15, 57.90 and 58.35 cents.
